violations.constraint: Consent accept/decline is never a chat-rendered control actuated by channel identity alone
violations.where: contract §6.1 (WidgetIntent: `requires: ConfirmationRequirement | null` — "non-null iff effect ∈ {REQUEST_APPROVAL, COMMIT}"; `capability` — "MUST be null iff effect ∈ {NONE, NAVIGATE, HANDOFF}") against §6.8 NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED, §9.1 ladder step 3, §11 Gate 4, INV-8
violations.why: The consent split's entire claimed structural defence is unrepresentable in the contract's own type system. §6.8 says the eight NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED capabilities have HANDOFF as "their only legal intent" and that each "additionally declares required_verification: SESSION_VERIFIED | STEP_UP_VERIFIED". But a HANDOFF intent must have `requires === null` (so there is no `required_verification` field to declare) and `capability === null` (so there is no capability name to match against the list). Gate 4 compares `verification_level >= requires.required_verification` — vacuous when `requires` is null. Ladder step 3 fires on `requires.required_verification > verification_level` OR `capability in NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED` — neither predicate can evaluate true for a HANDOFF intent. So on a CHANNEL_IDENTITY channel (Telegram, push) both the floor check and the list check are inert for exactly the intents that carry consent and identity-unbind actions, and the landing surface is unconstrained (see the separate HANDOFF-target finding). The claim in the winner rationale that "a channel-identity tap physically cannot actuate a 152-FZ decision" is false as specified.
violations.fix: Make `requires` (or at minimum `required_verification`) mandatory on HANDOFF as well as REQUEST_APPROVAL/COMMIT, and add a non-null `handoff_capability_ref` (registry key, non-actuating) so both Gate 4 and the NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED predicate can evaluate. Add an invariant: a CONSENT_STATE or IDENTITY_BINDING envelope is refused at emission unless every intent carries an explicit verification floor of SESSION_VERIFIED or above and a resolvable `s/<shell_route>` target.

violations.constraint: UI EVENT -> TYPED USER INTENT -> AUTHORITY VALIDATION -> CANONICAL OWNER with no shortcut; consent never actuated by channel identity alone
violations.where: contract §6.1 `ConfirmationRequirement.required_verification`; §11 Gate 4; §9.1 ladder step 3; IA §4.1–4.2 (Notifications as a chat SETTINGS_DRAFT)
violations.why: `required_verification` is a field the emitter authors onto the intent at mint time. Nothing in the contract binds it to the capability registry, to `AiToolPolicyService`, or to a risk tier — §6.8 says NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED capabilities "declare" it, i.e. by authorship. Gate 4 therefore validates the session against a number the mint path chose, not a server-derived floor, so the ladder's protection is only as strong as every future composer. Concretely: per-moment notification delivery preferences are communication-consent decisions (`Origin.notify_pref_key` is described as "the channel-consent key that gated this emission"), IA §4.1 explicitly says the Notifications surface "also is one, in chat" as a SETTINGS_DRAFT whose apply_intent is a COMMIT, and notification consent is not on the NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED list. A composer that declares `required_verification: 'CHANNEL_IDENTITY'` on that COMMIT produces a chat-rendered marketing/communication-consent control actuated by a Telegram tap, and it passes every stated invariant.
violations.fix: Derive the floor server-side: `required_verification = max(registry.minVerification(capability), policy.minVerification(riskTier))`, computed at mint and again at Gate 4; treat any emitter-supplied value as a hint only (the same treatment already given to `authority_hint`). Classify every consent-bearing capability — including per-moment notification preferences — in the registry with a minimum of SESSION_VERIFIED.

violations.constraint: No BUTTON -> DATABASE BUSINESS MUTATION; widgets are never a system of record
violations.where: contract §5.2 FORM row ("effect ceiling DRAFT / COMMIT"); §5.2 B2; §6.1 `InputSchema`; §11 Gate 12; §7 taxonomy (FORM owners include `loyalty.internal.adjust`)
violations.why: FORM is the one kind that accepts free-form, non-domain-closed input (`string`, `number`, `date`, `time`, `phone` with only length/pattern caps) and it may carry a COMMIT for an inherited capability. The taxonomy names `loyalty.internal.adjust` and `expenses.create` as FORM owners. A FORM tap therefore delivers a client-authored magnitude straight into Gate 12 as "resolved arguments" — a direct business mutation whose value the user supplied. The two headline safety mechanisms do not cover it: handles-as-nouns protects `frozen_nouns` only, and `inputs` are values by construction; the closed `selection_domain` applies only to `enum`/`ref`. The only control is the `FormJustification` enum, which §5.2 B2 itself concedes is "a social control, not a technical one". The contract's claim that "a widget cannot express a direct business mutation" is therefore false for the single largest mutation surface it defines.
violations.fix: Cap FORM at DRAFT: a FORM submission produces a server-owned draft that is re-rendered as a confirmation body (BOOKING_CONFIRMATION / SETTINGS_DRAFT / a new VALUE_CONFIRMATION), and only that body may carry the COMMIT — the same non-existence argument already used for booking. Additionally require every numeric/financial FORM field to name a server-side bound (min/max/allowed-delta) drawn from the capability, so a client-supplied magnitude is validated against canonical policy rather than a regex.

violations.constraint: Only a final canonical confirmation causes a booking effect; widget click cannot bypass booking intent, B31/B32/B33 or verified Client authority
violations.where: contract INV-7 ("Action Engine ingress refuses non-confirmation sources for `appointments.own.create`"); §5.2 BOOKING_CONFIRMATION body; §6.4 I2(b); §5 Table A row 5
violations.why: The enforcement clause that makes I2(b) real names exactly one capability: `appointments.own.create`. The registry also exposes `appointments.own.reschedule` and `appointments.own.cancel`, which are booking effects by any reading. INV-7 permits a COMMIT token to exist on APPROVAL, SETTINGS_DRAFT and FORM bodies, and nothing refuses a reschedule or cancel COMMIT minted on one of those. Since §11 Gate 11 states B31/B32/B33 run inside the booking owner's DRAFT step, a reschedule COMMIT that never passes through a canonical draft never runs booking-intent normalization, Client-principal verification or confirmation identity. Worse, BOOKING_CONFIRMATION's body has no shape for cancelling an existing appointment (its `cancel_intent` cancels the draft, not the record), so cancellation has no legal confirmation home at all and must be minted somewhere INV-7's clause does not guard.
violations.fix: Extend the Action Engine ingress refusal to the whole `appointments.own.*` family and to any capability the registry marks as booking-class, keyed off a `booking_effect: true` registry flag rather than a hardcoded name. Add an explicit cancellation/reschedule confirmation body (or a `confirmation_subject: 'create'|'reschedule'|'cancel'` discriminator on BOOKING_CONFIRMATION) so every booking effect has exactly one canonical confirmation surface.

violations.constraint: No BUTTON -> PROVIDER directly; the provider owner alone touches the provider
violations.where: taxonomy §5 Table A row 22 and §6 (`PAYMENT_HANDOFF`, owner "`p4-06-yookassa-checkout-provider`, `gift-certificate-*-shadow` — shadow, not registered"; "Tips resolve through the native bridge", `MayaRuntime.openTipsURL`); contract §6 EffectClass HANDOFF; §11 Gate 11 ("HANDOFF -> signed deep link, no capability invoked")
violations.why: PAYMENT_HANDOFF's declared ceiling is HANDOFF, and HANDOFF terminates at Gate 11 without invoking a capability and without ever reaching Gate 12, where §11 states "The Action Engine — never the widget, chat or renderer — calls the provider owner". The tap's destination is a payment provider's checkout, or `MayaRuntime.openTipsURL` on the native bridge. That is a widget button reaching an external provider with no capability, no Action Engine, no `idempotency_key`, no receipt and no canonical owner — and the taxonomy is explicit that the owner is unregistered/shadow. Because HANDOFF intents are capability-null, INV-10's registry check is vacuous and P2 ('no button for a capability with no canonical owner') cannot fire either, so an unowned money path passes every invariant. The project's own documented double-payment gotcha is exactly the failure mode an idempotency-free provider handoff reproduces.
violations.fix: Do not model payment as HANDOFF-to-provider. Route it as a canonical capability: a DRAFT owned by a registered payment/commerce owner produces a confirmation body, the COMMIT reaches Gate 12, and the Action Engine (not the renderer, not the native bridge) initiates the provider session and owns the idempotency key and the receipt. Until `GAP-COMMERCE-GIFT` and the tips owner are registered, PAYMENT_HANDOFF must emit a LIMITATION with `capability_gap_ref` and no intent, per P2.

violations.constraint: UI EVENT -> TYPED USER INTENT -> AUTHORITY VALIDATION -> CANONICAL OWNER with no shortcut
violations.where: contract §6 EffectClass NAVIGATE/HANDOFF; §11 Gate 11; §7 `Presentation.fullscreen_detail.route_key`; IA §6 (four link classes)
violations.why: The contract has no field anywhere that names a NAVIGATE or HANDOFF target and no invariant that constrains it. IA §6 defines four link classes but never binds intent targets to them, and one of those classes — `…/c/<capability_key>?scope=…` — is defined as "exactly equivalent to typing the utterance", i.e. it invokes a capability. So a capability-null NAVIGATE or HANDOFF intent can carry a `c/` link and thereby invoke a capability that INV-6, INV-10 and Gate 6 all believe does not exist for that intent, because the contract validated `capability === null`. The link is also the escape hatch for the consent HANDOFF: nothing requires it to resolve to `s/<shell_route>` (the only class with a stated SESSION_VERIFIED floor).
violations.fix: Add a required, closed-shape `target` to NAVIGATE and HANDOFF intents — `{ class: 'w'|'i'|'c'|'s', ref }` — validate at emission that `c` targets are registry keys within the principal's authority and that consent/identity handoffs use `s` only, and log the class in RenderReceipt. Add an invariant: no intent may carry a free-form URL.

violations.constraint: UI EVENT -> TYPED USER INTENT -> AUTHORITY VALIDATION -> CANONICAL OWNER with no shortcut; no BUTTON -> DATABASE BUSINESS MUTATION
violations.where: IA §5.4 (six overlays re-expressed: `detail.cash.declaration`, `detail.expenses.intake`, four `detail.settings.*`); IA §5.1–5.2; contract §7 `fullscreen_detail`
violations.why: Fullscreen details are entered by a capability-null NAVIGATE and then are governed by nothing in this contract — no envelope, no intent tokens, no gates, no RenderReceipt. Yet the details enumerated are precisely the mutating surfaces: cash declaration, expense intake ("correction"), and four governed-settings editors. IA §5.2 even states a detail may change something and post a receipt line back into the timeline, conceding they cause effects. The design's own diagnosis of these overlays is that "their only authorisation is the bearer check inside each component's first fetch"; moving the mount from a query parameter into the router removes the URL-as-authorisation defect but leaves the effect path entirely unspecified, so the mandated command path holds for widgets and is simply undefined where the business mutations actually live. The same applies to `SETTINGS_DRAFT.editor_handoff_intent`, the mandated non-chat fallback editor, which is a NAVIGATE into an ungoverned editor with COMMIT-equivalent power.
violations.fix: State normatively that a fullscreen detail is a renderer of envelopes, not a second application: every mutating control inside a detail must be an intent from an envelope minted for that route, submitted through the same gateway and the same twelve gates. Add an invariant that no detail route may hold provider credentials, compose provider arguments, or call a business endpoint directly, and require details to declare their `source_capability` the way projectors do.

violations.constraint: Only a final canonical confirmation causes a booking effect; no shortcut from UI event to canonical owner
violations.where: contract §9.1 ladder step 8 (NOTIFICATION: "a COMMIT action is permitted only when risk_tier === 'low_write' && reversible === true") against §13 ("A COMMIT reachable in one tap from a selector, a push, or a spoken utterance without readback" is forbidden); §5.2 APPROVAL row
violations.why: The ladder permits and §13 forbids the same thing; as written, the permissive rule is the operative one because the ladder is what the server executes. A push action id is the intent token, so the path is tap -> gateway -> COMMIT -> Action Engine with no confirmation body rendered and no readback required (`requires_readback` is an authored flag, and step 8 does not demand it). The actuating principal is a device holding a push subscription — CHANNEL_IDENTITY. Because INV-7 confines COMMIT tokens to four kinds, the push card in question is most plausibly an APPROVAL, whose own safeguard — "consent-aware audience maths shown before the irreversible tap" — cannot be delivered inside the profile's own `max_body_chars: ~120`. The safeguard is structurally undeliverable in the one channel where the one-tap commit is permitted.
violations.fix: Delete the COMMIT exception from ladder step 8: NOTIFICATION profiles carry NAVIGATE and HANDOFF only, landing on the confirmation body inside a verified surface (the rule IA §6 already states for link carriers — "an intent carrier never fires on open"). If a low-risk reversible one-tap action is genuinely wanted, give it its own effect class with a server-derived floor, a mandatory audience_size of null, and an explicit registry opt-in per capability.

violations.constraint: UI EVENT -> TYPED USER INTENT -> AUTHORITY VALIDATION -> CANONICAL OWNER with no shortcut
violations.where: contract §5.2 PROGRESS row ("effect ceiling NONE + cancel"); §6 EffectClass NONE ("dismiss, expand, local"); §11 routing map (cancel -> `POST /api/orchestration/runs/:id/cancel`); INV-6
violations.why: Cancel is classed under an effect ceiling of NONE, which the contract defines as purely local and which INV-6 forces to `capability === null`. But the routing map sends it to a server endpoint that terminates a run and, via `runs/:id/cancel`, can abort in-flight execution. A server state change is therefore travelling under the one effect class exempt from the registry lookup (INV-10), from `maxSideEffectClass`, and from any capability-keyed authority derivation at Gate 6. Anyone who can replay a token for a widget they can see can stop another principal's run, bounded only by Gate 3's principal binding. The same mis-classification pattern applies to any future 'local' action that turns out to hit an endpoint.
violations.fix: Introduce a `CONTROL` effect class (or class cancel as REFINE) that carries a registry capability and is subject to Gate 6 and INV-10, and reserve NONE for intents whose handler is provably client-side (no gateway submission at all). Add an invariant: an intent with `effect: 'NONE'` may not appear in the routing map.

violations.constraint: Conversation history is never business/consent/booking state; UI event -> typed intent -> authority validation ordering
violations.where: contract §11 Gate 7 (lowering appends the utterance to the conversation) placed before Gate 9 (input validation and noun resolution)
violations.why: The lowered utterance is `render(utterance_template, selected labels)` with `{{selection}}` interpolated from the client's `inputs`, and it is written into the durable conversation as a USER turn before Gate 9 validates those inputs against `input_schema` (closed-enum membership, length, byte caps, `SECURE_SURFACE_ONLY` rejection). So input that Gate 9 will refuse — oversize, out-of-domain, or a `SECURE_SURFACE_ONLY` value the contract says must never be rendered in chat — has already been persisted into the transcript and, per C9Context, into the LLM's untrusted-text channel. With FORM's free-form fields this is a durable prompt-injection and PII-leak path into history that survives the refusal.
violations.fix: Move input validation and `SECURE_SURFACE_ONLY` rejection to before lowering (validate at Gate 5/6, lower at Gate 8/9), and lower only from server-side canonical labels resolved from the closed domain, never from raw client bytes.

violations.constraint: LLM never generates numbers for a chart; charts render canonical C7/C8 data
violations.where: contract §4.3 `Provenance.generated_by: 'canonical'` ("No body field is LLM-authored") against §7 R2 ("Prose in text_equivalent, speech.lead and REPORT.narrative may be model-composed"); §5.2 REPORT body `sections[].narrative`; §5.1 `Measure.basis`, `Cell.label`; INV-14
violations.why: Three defects compound. (1) The contract asserts a literal, `generated_by: 'canonical'`, glossed as "No body field is LLM-authored", and then permits `REPORT.sections[].narrative` — a body field — to be model-composed; the literal is therefore false and INV-17 enforces a false statement. (2) The numeral check is circular where it matters: `Cell.label` and `Measure.basis` are free strings inside the body, so a numeral a model put into a label trivially "maps to a Measure present in the body" and passes INV-14 while being model-authored. (3) The check is a numeral check, so quantities written in words ("выручка выросла вдвое", "треть клиентов") evade it entirely — and the design's own open question proposes whitelisting ordinals and compound tokens such as 'топ-3' and '2 из 4' to avoid false positives, which widens the same exemption.
violations.fix: Drop the `generated_by: 'canonical'` literal or scope it honestly to non-narrative fields. Mint `Cell.label` and `Measure.basis` from the server formatter like `text_equivalent` and cover them by `body_hash`. Constrain model-composed narrative to a template with named `Measure` slots so quantities cannot be free text, and extend the CI check to a word-number lexicon rather than a numeral regex.

violations.constraint: LLM never generates numbers for a chart; charts render canonical C7/C8 data
violations.why: `y` is a `Measure` and therefore inside the Cell/provenance/formatter discipline; `x` is untyped and is neither a Cell nor a Measure. Axis positions, bucket boundaries and category values are chart numbers, and as specified they carry no `state`, no `as_of`, no `evidence_refs`, no basis and no coverage by R2's formatter rule — while `axes.x.type` is only a type hint. Nothing in the contract stops `x` values from being composed rather than read from the C7/C8 dataset, and `rows_digest` digests the dataset, not the rendered points.
violations.fix: Type `points[].x` as `Cell<string | number>` (or a `Measure` where numeric) and extend INV-14's hash check to assert that the emitted series — both axes — reduce to `dataset_ref` + `rows_digest`, so a chart that does not derive from the canonical dataset cannot be emitted.

violations.constraint: Widget click cannot bypass verified Client authority or the canonical owner; no BUTTON -> DATABASE BUSINESS MUTATION
violations.where: contract §10 ("What a submission cannot contain: ... a record id, a price, a date, a staff id, a client id") and §13, against §6.1 `InputSchema.fields.type: 'enum'|'ref'|'string'|'integer'|'date'|'time'|'phone'|'boolean'` where `enum_values` exists only for `enum` and `ref`
violations.why: The contract states as a guarantee that a submission cannot contain a date, a price or free values, and then defines an input schema that accepts `date`, `time`, `integer`, `string` and `phone` with no closed domain — only length, pattern and byte caps. The guarantee is true for `enum`/`ref` and false for everything else. Reviewers and implementers reading §10/§13 will conclude that Gate 9's closed-domain check covers all inputs and will not add value-range validation for the types that carry the risk (an integer for a loyalty adjustment, a datetime for a reschedule, a phone for an identity correction).
violations.fix: Rewrite the guarantee to what is actually enforced ("a submission may carry only values drawn from a server-declared closed domain, or scalars within server-declared bounds"), and require every non-enum field to carry server-declared bounds (`min`/`max`, allowed window, canonical normalizer) validated at Gate 9 against the capability, not against a regex.

violations.constraint: Only a final canonical confirmation causes a booking effect; widget click cannot bypass booking intent or the provider owner
violations.where: taxonomy §7 refusals ("Drag-to-reschedule is `SCHEDULE` + a `DRAFT` intent, not a new kind") against §5 Table A row 6 and contract §5.2 SCHEDULE row (effect ceiling `REFINE / NAVIGATE`)
violations.why: Two normative statements in the same document conflict about the highest effect a SCHEDULE may mint. If the ceiling table wins, the taxonomy's stated resolution for the entire calendar/journal family is unimplementable; if the taxonomy note wins, a drag gesture on a schedule grid mints a DRAFT whose new start time is a client-supplied `time` input with no closed domain (see the InputSchema finding), against `appointments.own.reschedule`, which INV-7's enforcement clause does not cover. An unresolved contradiction on an effect ceiling is exactly the kind of ambiguity that gets resolved at implementation time in favour of the feature.
violations.fix: Resolve explicitly in the contract: SCHEDULE stays at REFINE/NAVIGATE, and a drag emits a REFINE that returns a BOOKING_CONFIRMATION (reschedule variant) produced by the canonical booking owner with B31/B32/B33 run, on which alone the COMMIT is minted. Record the resolution in both the ceiling table and the taxonomy refusal row.

violations.constraint: Conversation history is never business state; widgets are never a system of record
violations.where: contract §8 ("Cross-channel resolution … Resolving in any channel resolves all"; `proactive_once`: "once acted on, resolved (\"Приду ✓\")"); `Lifecycle.resolution`; INV-11
violations.why: `resolution.state` lives in the envelope — the presentation layer. For `appointment_reminder`, INV-11 caps a proactive envelope at DRAFT, so a client tapping "Приду" produces no COMMIT and therefore no Action Engine receipt (§10 `action_receipt_ref` is null outside a canonical action). The design names no canonical owner for attendance confirmation. The only durable record that the client confirmed is `Lifecycle.resolution.state = 'resolved'` on the widget, which INV-15 then guarantees is deleted with conversation history. A staff member reading "клиент подтвердил" is reading widget state as business truth, and history erasure destroys it — the precise pattern the constraint forbids.
violations.fix: Either name a canonical owner for attendance/acknowledgement (an appointment-confirmation capability whose receipt is the record, with the envelope merely projecting it), or state normatively that `resolution` is delivery/presentation bookkeeping only and forbid any surface from presenting it as a client commitment. Cross-channel dedupe should resolve the *delivery*, not the business fact.

violations.constraint: Conversation history is never consent state; deleting history must leave canonical records correct (and must keep the erasure promise it makes)
violations.where: contract §8 Delete ("It never touches IntentRecords, Action Engine receipts …"); §6.2 `IntentRecord.utterance_template`; §10 `WidgetIntentSubmission.spoken_transcript` ("voice only, for audit"); §4.4 `GAP-HISTORY-ERASE`
violations.why: The contract presents "erasure never touches IntentRecords" as a safety guarantee, but IntentRecord and the submission record hold conversation-derived content: the `utterance_template` (the sentence the user is treated as having said), the selected labels interpolated into it, and the full `spoken_transcript` of voice turns. After a user exercises the right to erasure over conversation content, their utterances and voice transcripts remain, keyed to `principal_proof_hash`. That converts a stated 152-FZ capability into a promise the system does not keep — structurally the same defect as `/unsubscribe` promising a revocation that does not exist, which §4.4 exists to prevent.
violations.fix: Classify IntentRecord fields explicitly: authority-and-audit fields (hashes, capability, effect, timestamps, receipt refs) are retained; content fields (`utterance_template` renderings, selected labels, `spoken_transcript`) are conversation content and are erased or tombstoned with it. State the retention split in the contract before any erasure control is offered, and make it part of the `GAP-HISTORY-ERASE` owner's definition of done.

violations.constraint: Widget click cannot bypass the Action Engine or the canonical owner; only a final canonical confirmation causes a booking effect
violations.where: contract §6.3 I2(a) handles-as-nouns; §11 Gate 9 (fresh read at submission) and Gate 12 / APPROVAL path (`PENDING -> APPROVED -> COMPLETED`)
violations.why: The load-bearing anti-staleness graft is applied at Gate 9 to the *widget submission's* frozen nouns. An approval-gated action is different: the ActionExecution is created at REQUEST_APPROVAL time with its arguments already resolved, and the approver's later tap moves the state machine to APPROVED, after which execution proceeds against arguments frozen minutes or hours earlier. The contract never states that the canonical owner re-resolves nouns at execute time on the approval path. So "the price shown 90 seconds ago is never the price charged" and "a slot someone else took cannot be committed" hold for direct commits and silently do not hold across the approval boundary — which is the path deliberately used for the highest-risk and largest-audience actions.
violations.fix: Require the noun-resolution fresh read and SUPERSEDED/diff outcome at execute time on the approval path as well, not only at submission; if a noun has diverged since approval, the execution must return SUPERSEDED and re-enter approval with the diff rendered, rather than executing on stale values.

violations.constraint: No BUTTON -> PROVIDER; widgets are never a system of record; only a final canonical confirmation causes a booking effect
violations.where: contract open question 3 (`hold_token`, "a soft lock YClients does not own", specified as OPTIONAL/default-off) and §5.2 TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR `availability: Cell<'FREE'|'HELD'|'TAKEN'>`
violations.why: The HELD state is already in the shipped body shape, so the mechanism is half-present rather than deferred. If `hold_token` is enabled, a tap on a selector — a kind whose ceiling is DRAFT and about which §11 Gate 11 says "no business effect is reachable from a selector" — creates a real occupancy effect on a single-salon calendar. Because the provider does not own the lock, the widget layer becomes the system of record for who holds a chair, which is the one thing the constraints forbid outright, and a phantom hold has no canonical owner to reconcile or expire it.
violations.fix: Drop `hold_token` and rely on the SUPERSEDED-at-confirm outcome the handles-as-nouns graft already provides (the open question notes this is now cheap). Remove `HELD` from the availability enum unless and until the provider owns the hold, so the contract cannot express a lock nothing canonical holds.

violations.constraint: UNKNOWN must never be rendered as failure (the Cell discipline the rest of the safety argument leans on)
violations.where: contract §4.1 ("There is no bare number, string, boolean or date in any body field that reaches a user's eyes") against §5.1–5.2: `OptionItem.label/sublabel/badges`, `TableSpec.columns[].label`, `BOOKING_CONFIRMATION.lines[].label/detail` and `policy_notices`, `SETTINGS_DRAFT.diff[].from/to/effect_text`, `STRATEGY_OPTIONS.title/reasoning`, `FormField.label/help`, `SOURCE_STATUS.impact_text`, `LIMITATION.headline/detail`
violations.why: The universal-Cell rule is stated absolutely and then contradicted by most of the contract's own bodies, including the fields most likely to be unknown at render time: a settings diff's `from`/`to` (where a missing prior value renders as empty or an em dash — both explicitly forbidden as UNKNOWN renderings), a confirmation line's `detail`, and a staff label in a masked schedule. The renderer conformance suite (M2, five branches per Cell) cannot protect a field that is not a Cell, and INV-4/INV-5 (`reason_code` and `unknowns_sentence` required for any non-KNOWN Cell) simply do not fire for bare fields, so the minted text equivalent will confidently omit an unknown it has no state for.
violations.fix: Either make the rule real — convert every user-visible body field to `Cell<T>` and let the conformance suite and INV-4/INV-5 cover them — or narrow §4.1 to the fields it actually governs and add an explicit allowlist of server-authored constant strings, so implementers know which fields have no UNKNOWN protection.

unproven: "A channel-identity tap physically cannot actuate a 152-FZ decision" and "the VerificationLevel ladder ... makes the adversarially-corrected consent split structural" — unprovable as specified: HANDOFF intents carry neither a capability nor a `requires`, so both the Gate 4 floor and the NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED predicate are inert for exactly those capabilities.

"A COMMIT token for a booking does not exist anywhere at the moment a slot picker is rendered ... enforced by non-existence rather than by a check" — the enforcement is a check, and it is scoped by name to `appointments.own.create`; reschedule and cancel are unguarded.

"the forbidden edges are unrepresentable rather than forbidden" / "A widget cannot express a direct business mutation" (§11 forbidden-edges table) — false for FORM, which may carry COMMIT with client-authored values, and for PAYMENT_HANDOFF, which reaches a provider.
`Provenance.generated_by: 'canonical'` glossed as "No body field is LLM-authored" — contradicted by R2, which permits model-composed `REPORT.sections[].narrative`, a body field.

INV-14 / R2 "every numeral in rendered text maps to a Measure" — circular for numerals inside `Cell.label` and `Measure.basis`, blind to worded quantities, and further weakened by the open question's own proposal to whitelist ordinals and compound tokens.
"a server-derived floor at Gate 4" — `ConfirmationRequirement.required_verification` is authored at mint time with no registry binding; only the *actual* `verification_level` is server-derived.

"Deleting conversation history ... never touches IntentRecords" presented as a guarantee — it is a retention hole: IntentRecord holds `utterance_template` and submissions hold `spoken_transcript`, both conversation content.

"renderers provably cannot reach the network" (Glass Pane graft rationale) — the design concedes the correct verb is "discouraged": lint plus a bundle-graph check in a repository whose shipping frontend is a hand-edited single file with no build pipeline.

"one capability, three front doors, one function" with deterministic pre-LLM resolution (I5/I7) — asserted for typed and spoken free text, never demonstrated; the divergence gate that would measure it ships in shadow mode with no promotion criterion.

INV-16 capability parity as "the only gate that may authorise a deletion" — no evidence that the 669-disposition inventory is machine-readable or that a KEEP disposition can be mechanically matched to a widget kind, route or text intent.
"291 raw strings → 22 canonical types" as a total function — the 291 are not enumerated anywhere in the design, so neither totality nor the absence of a 23rd required kind is checkable.
"the registry resolves to 56 entries ... not 57" — a factual correction asserted against the brief; not verified in this review.

"1024-character intentToken cannot fit Telegram's 64-byte callback_data ... `w1.<widget10>.<intent6>.<sig8>` base62 ≈ 28–30 B" — the 8-byte signature's forgery resistance against an attacker who can enumerate widget/intent ids is asserted, not analysed.

Ladder step 8's premise that a `low_write` + `reversible` COMMIT is safe on a notification surface — `risk_tier` and `reversible` are copied or authored fields, and `reversible: true` is asserted by the source owner, not verified by the widget layer.
verdict: VIOLATIONS FOUND — the design does not satisfy the safety constraints as written. Nineteen violations, of which five are structural rather than editorial. The most severe is that the consent split has no mechanism at all: HANDOFF intents are required to carry `capability === null` and `requires === null`, so both of the protections the design relies on for 152-FZ decisions and identity unbinding — the Gate 4 verification floor and the NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED list check in ladder step 3 — are predicates that cannot evaluate true for the only intent class those capabilities are permitted to use. The claim that "a channel-identity tap physically cannot actuate a 152-FZ decision" is false as specified. Compounding it, `required_verification` is an emitter-authored field with no binding to the capability registry, so even where the floor is expressible it is not server-derived; and per-moment notification consent is a chat-emittable SETTINGS_DRAFT with a COMMIT apply, off the NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED list. Second, "a widget cannot express a direct business mutation" is false for FORM, which may carry COMMIT for an inherited capability (the taxonomy names `loyalty.internal.adjust`) with client-supplied non-domain-closed values; the only guard is a justification enum the design itself calls a social control. Third, the booking non-existence argument is enforced for exactly one capability name — `appointments.own.create` — leaving reschedule and cancel able to reach a COMMIT without a canonical draft and therefore without B31/B32/B33, with cancellation having no confirmation body at all. Fourth, PAYMENT_HANDOFF routes a tap to an unregistered external payment provider and the native tips bridge through HANDOFF, which terminates at Gate 11 without a capability, the Action Engine, an idempotency key or a receipt — a BUTTON -> PROVIDER edge that passes every invariant precisely because capability-null intents escape INV-10 and P2. Fifth, NAVIGATE and HANDOFF targets are untyped anywhere in the contract, and the fullscreen details those intents open (cash declaration, expense intake, four governed-settings editors) are governed by nothing in the design while hosting the actual mutations — the mandated command path is defined for widgets and undefined where the effects live. The design's honest register (§14) is genuine and several of its self-criticisms are correct, but none of the five above appear in it, and the two mechanisms the contract advertises as "enforced by non-existence rather than by a check" are each enforced by a check that is either name-scoped or unevaluable. The safety architecture is sound in intent and is defeated by its own type-level nullability rules; the fixes are local, not structural.
